Samir Patel: Heads-up — since the kernel-selection rollout yesterday we've observed ~22% of StatsD/OTel series for the runtime 'text.generate' route disappearing from the token-level latency dashboards. Looks like a tag/key mismatch in the pipeline.

Ella Zhou: Yep saw that on the per-route KPIs this morning. Token-latency breakdown has a gap for some kernel variants. Not all series, just a subset.

infra-bot: Alert: exporter-sync failed to write 503 -> upstream write error (2026-01-09T17:13:02Z)

Diego Torres: What changed in the PR? I remember a rename to disambiguate kernel tags — was it `kernel` -> `kernel_type`? If so queries that filter on `kernel=...` would no longer match new series.

Samir Patel: Correct. PR #4823 renamed the tag to `kernel_type` (intent: clarify quantized vs fp). Exporter change landed in prod but the StatsD collectors on some hosts still emit `kernel` only. The ingestion rules expect `kernel_type`. We end up with a set of metrics that never get aggregated into the dashboards -> appears as dropped.

Priya Nair: Can we remap in the OTLP/ingest layer? Add a copy rule: if `kernel` exists and `kernel_type` missing, set `kernel_type=kernel`. That would avoid re-ingest.

Ella Zhou: That would be the least disruptive short-term fix. But historical data still segmented across two tag keys. For accuracy of per-route KPIs we should backfill critical windows (last 7d).

Samir Patel: Plan I'm proposing:
1) Hotfix exporter -> emit both tags (`kernel` and `kernel_type`) for 48h. Patch and rollout ASAP.
2) Ingest shim: add compatibility mapping rule in OTLP receiver to copy `kernel`->`kernel_type` when missing. Short-lived, 72h max.
3) Targeted backfill for key routes (text.generate, chat.respond) over last 7 days into reindexed series. Keep scope narrow to avoid huge cost.

Samir Patel: Backfill command (prototype):
```bash
# run on backfill-runner (k8s job)
python tools/backfill_metrics.py \
  --s3-prefix s3://redwood-metrics/ingest/raw/2026-01-02_to_2026-01-09/ \
  --metric-filter "route in ('text.generate', 'chat.respond') and env=prod" \
  --tag-rewrite "kernel->kernel_type" \
  --output-prefix s3://redwood-metrics/backfill/reindexed/2026-01-09/
```

Diego Torres: How long will the backfill take at that granularity? If it replays at token-resolution, cost could be non-trivial.

Priya Nair: I can run a small dry-run for a single day and estimate. I expect ~2-3h for one day of `text.generate` given current runner size. I'll scale to 4 workers for the full 7d if acceptable.

Ella Zhou: Also add a dashboard sanity check after reindex: compare token-latency p50/p95 before and after for the affected kernel types and routes. I can add a regression alert to catch any variance >10%.

Samir Patel: Ownership:
- Samir -> exporter hotfix + deploy (ETA: 2h)
- Priya -> backfill dry-run + full run (ETA: dry-run 3h, full run tomorrow AM)
- Ella -> ingest shim + dashboard checks + regression alert (ETA: shim 1h, alert same day)
- Diego -> confirm queries/dashboards that need to switch to kernel_type vs accept mapped key (quick pass)

Samir Patel: Quick notes on why this happened so we don't repeat: the kernel renaming was safe for the runtime code paths but we didn't coordinate a metric compatibility plan (emit both tags or pipeline mapping) before flipping dashboards. Need a preflight checklist for tag/key renames: owner, compatibility window, exporter shim, backfill plan.

Priya Nair: Dry-run started: `backfill_metrics.py --days 1 --route text.generate --dry-run` -> ETA 10m. Will post results.

infra-bot: Deploy pipeline: hotfix-exporter v1.2.1 started (2026-01-09T17:18:40Z)

Samir Patel: Nice. Once hotfix is rolled I'll bump the ingest mapping to be lenient (copy kernel->kernel_type). After backfill we can deprecate `kernel` tag in 2 weeks.

Ella Zhou: Thx team :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: Dry-run complete. Estimated full 7d cost ~0.6 compute-hours per worker, recommended 4 workers -> ~2.4 compute-hours total. Starting full job in 45m. Logs and progress at: https://internal.jobs/backfills/1772345678

Diego Torres: I'll sweep dashboards and update query docs to prefer `kernel_type` and note the mapping.

Samir Patel: Closing loop: once backfill finishes, Ella will validate dashboards and flip the dashboards to read `kernel_type` as primary. Leave the exporter shim in place for 48h then remove.

Ella Zhou: Marking this thread as actionable. Reopen if any anomalies post-backfill.

Samir Patel: Thanks all.
